entries.title: Confirm Send no longer lists every additional contact under CC
entries.summary: With **Include additional contacts of recipients (CC)**, each recipient's additional contacts are copied on that recipient's own email. **Confirm Send** used to merge all of them onto one **CC** line, so a bulk send looked as if every email copied everyone. The **CC** line now shows only the addresses copied on every email, and the per-recipient copies appear as a count: "Additional contacts: N people CC'd on their own contact's email". Delivery was always correct; only the dialog changed.

where.path: Contacts or Sessions → select records → Send → Send Email → Include additional contacts of recipients (CC) → Review → Send Now

entries.use_case: A program team emails 120 speakers with each speaker's assistant CC'd. Confirm Send now reads "Additional contacts: 120 people CC'd on their own contact's email", not a CC line of 120 assistants that makes it look like every assistant gets every speaker's email.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer worries that a bulk email CC'd every additional contact on every message, or hesitates at Confirm Send because the CC line looks wrong.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who email speakers or contacts with their additional contacts (assistants, co-authors) CC'd.
internal.staff_path: Event → Contacts → select records → Send → Send Email → Include additional contacts of recipients (CC) → Review → Send Now
internal.gotchas: Display-only: emails always went out with each contact's own additional contacts only. A manually typed CC, or a CC that lands on every email, still shows on the CC line. With one recipient everything is listed as before. In Sessions → Select Individual Contacts, only checked recipients are counted. Reported by Clarion (event 6018, SB-10102).
internal.talk_track: What you see at Confirm Send now matches what goes out: each assistant is copied only on their own speaker's email.

entries.title: Session Catalog: choose a Catalog, Timetable or Agenda program layout — with a session panel, People directory and Add to calendar
entries.summary: A Session Catalog gallery now has a **Program layout** setting in the Design tab: **Catalog** (filter rail beside session rows grouped by day and time), **Timetable** (rooms across, start times down, colour-coded by track, with a Grid / List toggle) or **Agenda** (day tabs and expandable rows with Now / Next / Ended chips). Switching is instant in the preview. All three open the same session panel — date, time, room and time zone, abstract, speakers with bios, the presentations inside a symposium, **Save**, **Copy link** and **Add to calendar** (calendar file, Google Calendar, Outlook). A **People** tab adds a faculty directory with person pages. Sessions without a start time collect under a **TBA** day. The **Your brand** theme now keeps a neutral canvas and uses the brand colour for navigation and buttons, and the Site's font is loaded on every gallery.

enable.path: CMS → Content Galleries → a Session Catalog gallery → Design → Program layout

where.path: CMS → Content Galleries → a Session Catalog gallery → Design → Program layout / Navigation tabs → People

entries.use_case: A scientific congress with six rooms and three days wants attendees to scan the day room by room the way they do on the printed grid, and a single-track summit wants a phone-friendly agenda. Both are the same Session Catalog; the organizer picks Timetable or Agenda in Design and the published program, the session panel and Add to calendar come with it.

cs_action.note: Existing Session Catalogs keep the Catalog layout (the previous rows, now with the toolbar and day grouping). Offer Timetable to multi-room programs and Agenda to single-track or mobile-first ones; check the People tab is on if the customer wants a faculty page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer compares our program page to cAttendee, Oxford Abstracts or a custom program site, asks for a room-by-time grid, a day-tab agenda, speaker bios in the program, a faculty list, or Add to calendar on sessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Content Galleries preview customers publishing a Session Catalog — medical and scientific programs first.
internal.staff_path: Org → CMS → Content Galleries → a Session Catalog → Design → Program layout; super users can flip Demo mode (account menu) to preview every layout with a generated congress.
internal.gotchas: Timetable falls back to the list under 1024px and on the TBA day. Add to calendar appears only on sessions with a start time. Demo mode data shows only in the builder preview (preview token), never on the public URL. Program strings are English-only until the fr/es/de gallery translations ship. The Your brand theme change affects every gallery on that preset — the canvas is no longer the brand primary.

entries.title: Brella is generally available, and Apps is open to anyone who manages integrations
entries.summary: Brella no longer needs Sessionboard to add it: open **Apps** in the left sidebar, choose **Brella** under **Engagement**, and connect it yourself. **Apps** in the organization sidebar now shows to anyone who can view integrations, not only Sessionboard staff, and organization **Settings > Integrations** opens Apps.
entries.use_case: A customer running their event app on Brella can connect it the same day without a support ticket: their admin opens Apps, adds the Brella token and organization ID, and maps each Sessionboard event to a Brella event. Admins who used to go to Settings > Integrations land on Apps automatically.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for Brella, asks where Settings > Integrations went, or reports that Apps was locked for their admin.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations that use Brella for networking or content, and any admin who manages integrations.
internal.gotchas: LiveBuzz is still added by Sessionboard on request. Brella refuses a timeslot outside its event dates, so line those up before the first sync. Nothing is deleted in Brella: a speaker who leaves the accepted set comes off the timeslot and both records stay.
internal.talk_track: Brella is now a self-serve app. Open Apps from the sidebar, connect Brella with your token and organization ID, map your event, and sync.

entries.title: See every email an event will send before it goes out
entries.summary: **Email Campaigns → Upcoming sends** lists the next 7, 14 or 30 days of automatic email: scheduled and recurring campaigns, upload slot, acceptance, call for papers and awards reminders, the speaker feedback release, and date-based automations. Open a send to see each recipient and the email they will get, with a warning when it reaches people on unaccepted sessions. Two automatic sends that were failing now go out: date-based automations that skipped enrolled contacts, and the awards submission deadline reminder.
entries.use_case: Before a reminder goes out, a program manager can check exactly who receives it and what it says, and catch a send that would reach speakers on pending or declined sessions, instead of finding out from a confused speaker afterwards.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why someone got (or did not get) an automatic email, or wants to check reminders before a deadline.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event team using reminders, scheduled campaigns or automations.
internal.gotchas: The recipient list shows the first 500 people. Automations with no fixed time are listed separately as sends that fire when triggered.
internal.talk_track: Upcoming sends is one list of everything the event will email on its own. Open any send to see who gets it and preview the message.

entries.title: A guided wizard for new sites, galleries and embeds
entries.summary: **Create** on **Publish → Sites** — and **New site**, **New gallery** and **New embed** on the Publish overview — open one short wizard. Pick what you are making (**Marketing Site**, **Session Catalog**, **Media Gallery**, **ePoster Gallery** or **Embed**), name it and choose its web address (the host is shown, the address is checked as you type), then the layout, who can see it and its look. It only asks what that surface needs, and you land in the builder. A surface that is not on yet is greyed out with the reason and a button to turn it on or ask for it.

where.path: Publish → Sites → Create (or New site / New gallery / New embed on Publish → Overview)

entries.use_case: A marketing lead wants an on-demand library for last year's recordings. They click New gallery, pick Media Gallery, type a name and address, choose the On-Demand Hub layout and email-gated access, and land in a builder that is already set up — no blank page, no hunting through settings.

cs_action.note: Good moment to show customers who have put off building a gallery or site.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to start a site, gallery or embed, or which one they need.
internal.who_should_get_it: Anyone who publishes event content: marketing and program teams.
internal.staff_path: Org or event → Publish → Sites → Create
internal.gotchas: Each event has one marketing site, so on an event that already has one the Marketing Site card says Open the site. Gallery cards are locked until Content Galleries (Preview) is on; ePoster Gallery is locked until Poster Gallery (Beta) is on for the event — at org level, until any live event has it. Session Catalog and ePoster Gallery are per event, so at org level the wizard asks which event.
internal.talk_track: Tell it what you're making and it asks only what that needs, then drops you into a builder that's already set up.

entries.title: Publish: Sites, Embeds and Posters in the sidebar, live previews of every site
entries.summary: The Publish module is simpler. In an event it lists **Overview**, **Sites**, **Embeds** and **Posters** (plus **Floor Maps** when on); at the organization level, **Overview** and **Sites**. Galleries now sit on the **Sites** page under its **Galleries** tab, and every card shows a screenshot of that site's landing page, its own domain or address, and an open-in-new-tab button on hover. **Posters** is always listed and explains Poster Gallery on events that do not have it. The **Overview** gives each row its type icon, shows only the places an item is actually live, drops the empty Views column, renames **Lists** to **Embeds**, leaves out archived and deleted events, and adds **Configure SSO** and **Domains** buttons. In Program, **Collect & Review → Submission forms** is now just **Forms** in the sidebar.
entries.use_case: A program manager opens Publish → Sites and recognises each site from its screenshot instead of a list of slugs, and spots that last year's archived event no longer clutters the Overview.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer can't find Content Galleries or Poster Gallery in the sidebar, or asks where their galleries went.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with sites, galleries or embeds.
internal.gotchas: The Content Galleries list page still exists at /cms/galleries but has no sidebar row; galleries are reached from the Sites page. Screenshots are captured on first view (2–3 s) and refreshed when the site changes or after 12 hours; until then the card shows a layout sketch. Posters opens the Poster Gallery request page on events without it — it no longer has a lock.
internal.talk_track: Everything with its own address is on one page now, and you can see what each one looks like before you open it.

entries.title: Add Program: one page for conferences, awards, webinars and gatherings
entries.summary: **Add Event** is now **Add Program**, on the organization's **Events** page and under the **+** button. It opens a page that asks **What are you creating?** — **Conference**, **Awards**, **Webinar** or **Gathering** — with tidier basics (**Name**, **Starts**, **Ends**, **Time zone**, **Website**). Webinars and gatherings are marked **Beta** when your organization does not have them yet and show what they do with a **Request beta access** button instead of a form. **Awards** shows your plan's program allowance and **Start the awards wizard**, or **Add-on** with **Talk to us about Awards** when your organization does not have Awards.
entries.use_case: An events lead wants to try a webinar series. Add Program → Webinar shows what webinars do and a Request beta access button, instead of a form they cannot submit.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to add an event, webinar, gathering or awards program, or why they cannot create a webinar.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every org admin who creates events.
internal.staff_path: Org → Events → Add Program. Super users get a View as customer toggle, a staff-only Advanced panel (sandbox seeding) and Create anyway on gated kinds.
internal.gotchas: The Lite conference format is gone from this page. Webinar/Gathering need the gatherings Beta; requests for it go through Early Access. Super users see staff-only controls — use View as customer to demo it.
internal.talk_track: Pick what you are making and the page asks only what that needs — and tells you plainly when something needs to be turned on first.

entries.title: Conference requests ask the onboarding questions and reach Customer Success directly
entries.summary: When a new conference has to be set up by Customer Success, **Add Program** now sends a request that asks **Help us set it up**: what you manage (abstracts, sessions or both), roughly how many speakers and sessions, whether submissions are evaluated (rounds and evaluators), and when the call opens and closes — all optional. The confirmation, ready and declined emails come from the Customer Success team's address, so a reply reaches them. Customer Success sees the request, with those answers, the moment it is sent and can open it straight into a prefilled event form.

where.path: Events → Add Program → Conference → Send request

entries.use_case: A society contracted for one meeting requests a second. Their request says ~120 speakers, two evaluation rounds and a call closing 20 February, so their CSM can scope the contract change and set the event up toward those dates without a separate intake call.

cs_action.note: CS handles requests from the success@ inbox and the Event requests section of Admin → Onboarding intake; nothing to enable.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for a new event, or a single-event customer wants to add one.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who cannot create conferences themselves (most orgs).
internal.staff_path: Admin → Onboarding intake → Event requests → open a request → Open in Add Program form / Open in clone form → Create and fulfil request (or Decline, reason optional). The internal email to success@ has the same link; replying to it answers the requester.
internal.gotchas: There is no contract or entitlement check — any org member who can open Add Program can request, and the CSM decides. The setup questions are asked only for conferences, not webinars or gatherings. Fulfilling adds the requester to the event's team.
internal.talk_track: Tell us roughly what the event looks like when you ask for it, and your CSM can get it set up — and your plan sorted — without a separate call.

entries.title: Starting an awards program no longer errors when your plan has none left
entries.summary: Clicking **New Program** in Awards, or **Awards** on **Add Program**, used to show an error when your plan allowed no more awards programs. It now opens a panel that shows how many programs your plan includes and how many you have used, with **Start the awards wizard** — or, when none are left (or none are included yet), says so plainly and offers **Contact Customer Success**.

where.path: Awards → New Program (or Events → Add Program → Awards)

entries.use_case: An admin whose plan includes three awards programs, all used, sees "You've used all 3" and a way to contact their CSM, instead of an error that looks like a bug.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports an error when creating an awards program.
internal.who_should_get_it: Awards customers at or near their program allowance.
internal.staff_path: Org → Awards → New Program; the allowance is the org plan’s Max awards programs.
internal.gotchas: An org whose plan has Max awards programs empty or 0 sees "Your plan doesn't include awards programs yet" even with the Awards module on — raise the plan limit to let them create one. Starting the wizard needs the Create Awards permission.
internal.talk_track: If your plan is full, it tells you so and how to get more — no mystery error.

entries.title: Organization Home shows your upcoming events; the new dashboard is on for everyone
entries.summary: The organization's **Home** page now shows your upcoming events right under **Needs you**, each card a click into the event. The redesigned organization **Dashboard** is now on for every organization, not only those using Pathways; the Pathways and Topics cards still appear only when Pathways is on.
entries.use_case: An admin who runs six events a year opens Home and jumps straight into the one starting next week from its card.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks for a faster way into their events, or notices the dashboard changed.
internal.gotchas: The event dashboard is unchanged. Admin Settings (org and event) no longer list the retired Community, New Navigation, Setup Center and Briefs toggles — display only, their stored values are untouched.
internal.talk_track: Your next events are on Home, a click away.

entries.title: Domains lists only events that send from their own address
entries.summary: **Settings > Domains** at the organization level listed every event under **Event email addresses**, including events that simply use the organization's address. It now lists only events that send from their own address, and hides the table when none do.
entries.use_case: An admin checking which events need their own domain set up sees only the two events that send from their own address, not every event repeating the organization's address.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer is confused that every event appears to have its own sender address.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with a custom email domain.
internal.gotchas: Case or surrounding spaces do not make an address different. An event whose own domain setup is in progress still appears.
internal.talk_track: The list now shows only events that really send from somewhere else.
